newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan bill rates continue to rise in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan bill rates continue to rise in latest week.

text.p: Rates kept an upward thrust at Kenya's treasury bill auction despite a senior official saying that he saw a major decline towards the end of the year.
Average rates on the main 91-day body of treasury bills jumped to 24.272 percent compared to 23.577 percent in the previous week, the central bank said in a statement on Friday.
It said rates on the 28-day bills were stable, at 14.955 percent compared to 14.972 percent in the previous week.
Of the 8.0 billion shilling it offered in treasury bills, the central bank said 5.757 billion shillings was tendered.
The bank said it accepted 4.820 billion shillings from around 4.798 billion shillings in competitive bids and 21.70 million in non competitive bids at the average tender.

Some 31.85 billion shillings was tendered for 28-day bills of which 25.20 billion shillings was accepted. In the 91-day category, around 4.795 billion shillings was tendered and 4.775 billion shillings was accepted.
There were no offers for 182-day bills, as in last week.
There were a total of 383 bids, 234 successful, 89 unsuccessful and 60 non competitive. That compared to 395 bids last week of which 272 were successful, 53 unsuccessful and 70 non-competitive.
The bank invited tenders for 6.0 billion shillings in treasury bills for the next auction on Thursday next week.

On Thursday in Southampton, Bermuda, Finance Minister Musalia Mudavadi said Kenya's interest rates should ease by the end of this year. "We hope that by the end of the year the rate (on Treasury bills) will be down to 18 percent."
He did not say how that would be achieved.
The treasury bill auctions are held late on Thursdays. The central bank does not normally specify whether it was foreign or domestic investors who tendered for the bills.
